dmm-2012-relay-01.prompt: Kathleen and Andrew play a game. Kathleen has a probability $0<p<1$ of winning the game. Andrew notes that Kathleen's probability of winning a best-out-of-$3$ series of games is the same as her probability of winning an individual game. What is the probability that Kathleen wins an individual game?

dmm-2012-relay-02.prompt: Andrew wants to figure out which pairs of his friends are also friends. He decides to survey every one of his $F$ friends. It takes him $90$ minutes to set up the survey, and then $F$ minutes to give the survey to each of his friends. If $F=30$, what is the time per friend that Andrew spends on the survey, including set-up?

dmm-2012-relay-03.prompt: Let $T=11$. $ABCD$ is a square; $E$ is the midpoint of its diagonals, and $F$ is a point external to the square such that $\angle CFD$ is right. If $FD=T$ and $FE=12\sqrt2$, what is $FC$?

dmm-2012-relay-04.prompt: How many ways can the numbers $1$ through $6$ be assigned to the vertices of a hexagon such that no two consecutive numbers lie on adjacent vertices? (Two numberings are considered equivalent if one can be rotated into the other.)

dmm-2012-relay-05.prompt: A palindrome is a string that reads the same way forwards and backwards; for example, "abba" and "xyzyx" are both palindromes. For $n\ge1$, let $P(n)$ denote the number of palindromes of length $n$ using the $26$ letters of the English alphabet. Let $T=10$. Find $P(T+1)/P(T)$.
